media.title: Ufa-Theater Universum, Berlin — street façade, 1928
media.description: Street view of the curved façade and entrance of the Ufa-Theater Universum in Berlin, published in Mario von Bucovich’s photographic volume Berlin in 1928. The image documents the venue before Bick & Kaper’s documented appearance there in February 1929; it does not depict that performance or constitute evidence of Kaper’s presence in the photographed scene.
media.altText: Black-and-white street photograph of the curved façade and entrance of the Ufa-Theater Universum in Berlin, with signs on the building and pedestrians on the pavement.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in Mario von Bucovich’s Berlin (Berlin: Albertus Verlag, 1928). Whether its term is counted from the death of the named photographer or, as for an anonymous work, seventy years from publication, it was still protected in Germany on 1 January 1996, so the URAA restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication; that term ran out at the end of 2023. Wikimedia Commons applies the Public Domain Mark 1.0 to the digital reproduction.

timelineEvents.title: Move to Berlin
timelineEvents.label: c. 1926 · Move to Berlin
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper left Warsaw for Berlin to continue his musical education and professional development.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Around 1926, Kaper left Warsaw for Berlin to continue his musical education. The manuscripts date the move to that year: the Piece for Orchestra of 1926 is headed “written in Warsaw”, while the song Hätt’ ich einen Kammerdiener?, also of 1926, is listed in the collection’s accession list as written in Berlin. By his own account he came intending to enrol at the Hochschule für Musik.

places.publicNote: Historic cinema site at Kurfürstendamm 153, connected with the 1929 Bick & Kaper appearance at the premiere of Der Adjutant des Zaren. The marker identifies the documented venue site, not a position within the former auditorium.
